newsitem.title: INDIA: UN Secretary-General to visit India from April 7.
newsitem.headline: UN Secretary-General to visit India from April 7.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan is scheduled to arrive in India on April 7 for a three-day official visit, Indian Foreign Ministry officials said on Thursday.
They said Annan would visit India for the ministerial conference of the Non-Aligned Movement, being held in New Delhi on April 7 and 8.
Annan is scheduled to hold talks with Indian leaders during his visit, they said.
Indian Foreign Minister Inder Gujral is due to meet his Pakistani counterpart, Gohar Ayub, on the sidelines of the same conference.
Top-level talks between the two neighbours, which have gone to war three times since independence from Britain in 1947, are scheduled to resume on March 28 after breaking down in 1994.
Islamabad says it hopes to discuss the disputed territory of Kashmir, of which India controls two-thirds and Pakistan the rest.
The dispute has been pending at the United Nations since 1948, when India and Pakistan fought their first war.
India says the Kashmir dispute should be discussed under a 1972 agreement between the two neighbours, while Pakistan says the pact does not preclude a U.N.-sponsored plebiscite.
It was not immediately clear whether Annan would discuss the issue with Indian officials.
